Approved evidence

Post-Training on Office Work Improves Software Engineering: A Behavioral Account of Cross-Domain Transfer

paper.arxiv.2608.01604

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2608.01604v1. Outcome-conditioned paired trajectory analysis and no causal/domain-matched counterfactual establish a distinct behavioral analysis of connected training. It is not collapsed with2608.00181or counted as an independent experiment. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

full source

included

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

All results come from one model/training run. No task-demand ablation or equal-budget software-training counterfactual was performed; outcome-conditioned examples and analyst-selected explanations cannot establish a causal mechanism, prevalence of capabilities or that office training is the most efficient path to SWE improvement.

repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2608.01604.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • The study uses 363 office/general-tool training tasks, deterministic Python final-state criteria, 3,000 selected Kimi K2.6 warmup trajectories and SFT followed by GSPO on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B.
  • Claude Opus 4.8 assists root-cause reports that authors manually check against raw trajectories. The analysis selects 103 base-fail/trained-pass tasks and does not estimate general capability prevalence.
  • Retrieval-span overlap, reference-patch overlap, patch size and formal-test commands are indirect behavioral proxies. Reference patches are not unique ground truth; all results use one model/training run without task-demand ablation or an equal-budget software-training counterfactual.
  • This paper describes reward as trajectory-level criterion fraction. Companion 2608.00181v1 additionally reports a low-score effort floor and Toolathlon-informed initial family/teacher choice; the two protocol descriptions are not silently equated.
  • Matching model, 363-task/3,000-trajectory recipe and reported values suggest shared experimental provenance with 2608.00181v1. This is an author inference; the work identities remain separate and independent experimental replication is not established.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The study describes a combined SFT-plus-GSPO post-training experiment on 363 LHMTA office/general-tool tasks, followed by analysis of 103 base-fail/trained-pass task pairs using Claude Opus 4.8-assisted reports manually checked against raw trajectories. This is an outcome-conditioned analysis, not a random sample of all agent behavior.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

For the same base/trained checkpoints, Table 3 reports greedy SWE-BenchPro pass@1 changing from 20.5% to 26.3%. Over 731 paired SWE tasks, Table 5 separately reports the share containing a formal-test command changing from 37.5% to 73.3%; test invocation is an indirect behavior measure and does not establish semantic correctness.
